html:
Salvador Allende was the president of Chile from 1970 until he died in the military coup of 11 September 1973. He was the first Marxist elected president in Latin America.

A doctor and a founder of the Socialist Party, he ran for president four times. In 1970 he won with about a third of the vote, leading a left-wing coalition, Popular Unity. He nationalised the copper mines and banks, sped up land reform and raised wages.

The United States, which feared another Cuba, worked to undermine him. Inflation soared, shortages spread, and Chile split into hostile camps, with strikes by truck owners and shopkeepers. On 11 September 1973 the armed forces attacked the presidential palace, and Allende took his own life inside. The coup brought Augusto Pinochet to power in Chile.
sum: Salvador Allende was the president of Chile from 1970 until he died in the military coup of 11 September 1973. He was the first Marxist elected president in Latin America.
